title: Quantum detection of CP violation in the $t\bar{t}$ system: tomography
authors: Priyanka Lamba, Fabio Maltoni, Olimpia Miniati, Eleni Vryonidou
abstract: We develop a quantum-tomographic framework for determining whether possible CP-odd effects in $t\bar t$ events originate in production, in decay, or in both. In the narrow-width approximation, the process $I\to t\bar t\to b\ell^+ν\,\bar b\ell^-\barν$ factorises into a production density matrix and top and antitop decay density matrices. We extend the standard tomography procedure to a general anomalous $Wtb$ vertex and derive the corresponding angular distributions. Polar-angle distributions retain their usual tomographic form, up to modifications of the spin-analysing powers, and can therefore be used to reconstruct the production density matrix and test its CP properties. By contrast, dedicated azimuthal observables involving the $b$--lepton decay planes contain characteristic sine modulations that provide linear probes of possible new CP-violating interactions in the decay vertex. Combining the two classes of observables gives a systematic strategy for separating sources of CP violation in production and in decay. We illustrate the resulting angular signatures for representative $t\bar t$ production scenarios at hadron and lepton colliders.
summary: This paper presents a sophisticated quantum-tomographic method to search for CP violation in $t ar{t}$ production. It systematically separates potential new physics sources by analyzing two distinct classes of angular observables: polar angles (for production) and azimuthal angles involving decay planes (for decay). The framework is powerful because it provides a comprehensive diagnostic tool for future collider experiments.
main_problem: The goal is to develop a quantum-tomographic framework to definitively determine whether observed CP-odd effects in $t ar{t}$ events originate from the production mechanism, the decay vertex, or both.
main_result: By combining measurements of polar-angle distributions (probing production) and azimuthal observables involving $b$-lepton decay planes (probing decay), a systematic strategy is established to separate these sources of CP violation.
model_or_system: The system is top-antitop quark pair production ($t ar{t}$) followed by leptonic decay. The framework utilizes the narrow-width approximation, factorizing the process into a production density matrix and individual top/antitop decay density matrices, which are analyzed using Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) corrections to the $Wtb$ vertex.
key_observables: Polar-angle distributions (reconstruct $ho_I$) and azimuthal observables involving $b-\ell$ decay planes (show sine modulations for decay CPV).
important_parameters: The analysis is sensitive to anomalous couplings in the $Wtb$ vertex, tested at various collider energies ($\sqrt{s}=365 	ext{ GeV}$ mentioned for $e^+e^-$).
main_assumptions: The narrow-width approximation is employed throughout the calculation. Leptons are assumed massless.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the factorized spin-density-matrix description, then deriving decay matrices incorporating anomalous couplings, followed by deriving the angular distributions necessary for tomography, and concluding with a discussion of the combined measurement strategy.
why_interesting: While focused on particle physics, the methodology—using quantum state tomography to disentangle sources of non-Hermitian or CP-violating information encoded in correlations—is highly relevant to open quantum systems theory and characterizing decoherence channels.
